# Architecture

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/generate_documents.py; edit source records instead. -->


## Shared Python game-state architecture

### Decision: Board, moves and rule evaluation are separate

`engine.model.game.board.Board` owns a rectangular matrix of optional piece objects, capture lists and placement/movement/replacement operations. Its built-in `setup_default_board` populates standard chess pieces on an 8×8 board. `engine.model.pieces` contains the concrete chess classes: Pawn, Rook, Horse, Bishop, Queen and King.

`engine.model.game.move.Move` stores origin, destination, move type, optional moving/captured/promoted pieces. `Move.validate` checks coordinate bounds (currently fixed at 8×8), origin occupancy and destination friendly-piece conflicts. `Move.execute` invokes `Board.move_piece` and optional destination replacement. Declared move types are metadata; execution is not a full general-purpose rules interpreter.

`MoveValidator` implements chess-oriented pseudo/legal moves, detection of king attacks/check, and checkmate/stalemate. `GameManager` owns `Board`, players with `1/-1` colors, active turn, `Timer`, `MoveValidator` and `GameLogger`. Its `make_move` validates the move and player, executes it, records it and changes the active side. Its state evaluation covers active-player timeout, checkmate, stalemate, check and in-progress. `save_log` remains a stub.

### Decision: supporting game state stays modular

`Timer` holds two time balances and exposes reset/tick/increment/expiry. `Quest` holds condition callback, completion flag and reward points; `engine.model.misc.quest_manager.QuestManager` stores/evaluates quests and may award completion to a `User`. `engine.model.users` holds identity/rating/history; `engine.model.misc` also implements coordinate notation, PGN-style metadata and chess export helpers; `GameLogger` tracks moves in memory with optional output.

### Data flow

`GameController.handle_square_click` → `GameManager.make_move` → `MoveValidator.is_valid_move` → `Move.execute` → `Board.move_piece` → `GameLogger.log_move` → change active player. The controller returns an action descriptor and current game state.

### Current limitation

The in-memory engine is chess-centric and its declarative checkers configuration does not itself provide complete English-draughts gameplay. The Python process owns this state in memory.

_Source: [0001-components.md](decisions/0001-components.md)_


## Game configuration and package discovery

### Decision: installed entry points own the game registry

`pyproject.toml` installs the `engine`, `chess`, `checkers` packages under `packages/`. The `boardgameswithquests.games` entry-point group registers named game packages. `engine.model.game.configuration` iterates registered entry points using `importlib.metadata`, loads each package's `config.json` through `importlib.resources` and returns immutable `GameDefinition` dataclasses. It rejects duplicate/mismatched names, malformed records, and multiple declared defaults.

### Current configuration format

A `schema_version: 1` definition has `name`, `title`, boolean `default` and `playable`, `board` with row/column dimensions and starting-piece placements, `pieces` with colors/symbols/movement and attack vectors/jump/repeat flags, `clock` with starting/increment seconds, `exports` and `appearance`. The loader checks valid dimensions (1–256), unique in-bounds positions, declared pieces, two colors, nonzero integer vectors, nonnegative times and field types.

`packages/chess/config.json` describes initial chess pieces and vector metadata. `packages/checkers/config.json` describes English-draughts men and kings and their layout. Both describe 8×8 boards; both currently set `playable: false`. Configuration discovery/validation is implemented; transforming this metadata into a complete playable rules engine is **not** yet implemented.

### Ownership consequence

`engine.model.game.games` supplies available/default game names and package paths. Game-specific data remains with installed packages; shared validation belongs to the engine. A future implementation must update this decision if the JSON/runtime ownership changes.

_Source: [0002-configuration.md](decisions/0002-configuration.md)_


## Application entry and controller boundary

### Current entry points

`pyproject.toml` maps the `chesswithquests` GUI script to `engine.app:main`; `python -m engine` delegates to the same function. It parses `--game` and `--check`. The latter prints installed game readiness without opening a display. Normal launch resolves a named/default registered `GameDefinition`, rejects invalid or `playable: false` games, then attempts `tkinter.Tk()` and `engine.view.app.build_application`. Missing Tkinter, display failure and missing view produce separate error paths. The existing `engine.view` package is a placeholder interface, not a completed GUI.

### Controller interactions

`GameController` owns the `GameManager`, selected square and highlighted valid destinations. `select_square` checks active-player piece ownership; `handle_square_click` distinguishes selected/reselected/moved/invalid/none and reports move origin/destination and resulting state. `new_game` replaces the manager and clears UI selection state.

`WindowController` stores nominal window title/dimensions, running state, status message and an active dialog message. It dispatches clicks to `GameController`, updates status text and ticks the active player's clock. It is state/controller logic rather than Tkinter widgets.

### Responsibility boundary

`engine.app` owns startup and game selection; controllers own interaction state. The installed view interface does not provide a playable Tkinter application.

_Source: [0003-application.md](decisions/0003-application.md)_


## Documentation, automation and release architecture

### One source per kind of information

The independently authored `.agents/GOAL.md`, `PLAN.md`, `TODO.md` and `SCRATCHPAD.md` contain product outcomes, phase plan, current action queue and temporary investigation notes. They are not generated.

`.github/scripts/generate_documents.py` derives `.agents/README.md` from published `notes/`, `PRD.md` from approved `requests/`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` from accepted `decisions/`, and `AGENTS.md` from active `rules/`, with deterministic ordering/backlinks. GitHub CI checks generated files; root README/CONTRIBUTING are symlinks. `.agents/architecture/diagrams/` contains source-generated Mermaid diagrams; preserved original references live in `.agents/reference/`.

### Native GitHub and DarkFactory ownership

Real root `.github/workflows/`, `scripts/`, `tests/` own Actions, document generation, and all repository tests. `.agents/agents/` and `skills/` define role-specific instructions. `.darkfactory/installation.json` and `repo.dfconfig` record the DarkFactory integration, PrideVer release versioning, and stated branch/release policy.

`develop` is the integration branch, `main` the intended release branch. `main-source.yml` verifies that a PR targeting `main` originated from `develop` in the same repository; actual GitHub native protection requires provider-side enforcement, not merely source configuration.

### Guarded desktop packaging and publication

`desktop-build.yml` defines Windows x64, macOS ARM64/x64, and Linux x64 native jobs. `package_desktop.py` builds a PyInstaller distribution, verifies that a frozen executable remains running for the smoke interval, and archives it with SHA256 sidecars. It resolves distribution identity from `pyproject.toml` on Python 3.10–3.13 and rejects missing or altered frozen game resources. `release.yml` checks the exact live `main` commit, refuses disabled Python release publication, requests an authoritative PrideVer version, depends on the native matrix and verifies all four assets/checksums before publishing a new draft as public. Existing published releases and drafts are rejected rather than overwritten or reused.

These are **implemented automation files**, not evidence that a complete GUI application has yet been packaged. Python publication is disabled; the installed engine entry point does not provide a playable GUI.

_Source: [0004-repository.md](decisions/0004-repository.md)_
